name: Georgi Petrov (synthetic)

facts.label: lay tiles
facts.story: Tiles bathrooms and kitchens in renovations of apartment buildings, from removing the old tiles to silicone.

facts.label: plan tiling
facts.story: Plans the layout before cutting and teaches his employee to measure first.

facts.label: apply tile adhesive
facts.story: Chooses flexible adhesive for old floors and back-butters large-format tiles.

facts.label: fill tile joints
facts.story: Grouts and seals joints and expansion joints as part of the whole job.

facts.label: cut tiles
facts.story: Cuts with a wet saw and tile cutter to fit around drains and corners.

answers.recent_work: I've been tiling bathrooms and kitchens for twenty-two years, the last nineteen in Finland, mostly renovations in apartment buildings around Espoo. I do the whole job: remove the old tiles, check the floor, waterproofing, then laying, grouting and silicone. I'm 49, I came from Bulgaria in 2007 as a tiler, and I run my own small tiling company with one employee.
answers.example: A bathroom in a 1970s building had a floor that sloped away from the drain in one corner, and the old tiles were cracking. I took everything up, measured the slope with a long level, and levelled the screed to give a proper fall to the drain. Then I put in a waterproofing membrane, tested it with water for twenty-four hours, and tiled over it. The customer called a year later to say it was still dry.
answers.tools: Tile cutter, wet saw, notched trowels, a levelling system and a laser level. For waterproofing I use the membrane system and I hold the wet room certificate, so the work gets documented properly. The adhesive depends on the tile size and the floor: flexible adhesive on old floors, and big tiles need back-buttering.
answers.people: Most of my customers are housing companies and private owners, and I work with the plumber and the electrician in the same bathroom, so we agree the order of work. My employee is in his second year and I teach him how to measure and plan the layout before cutting. The customer decides the tile, I decide how it's installed.
answers.beyond: I went to a vocational school for construction in my home country. Here I took the wet room course and the occupational safety card. I also fix small things in the housing company where I live, like cracked tiles in the stairwell, for free.
answers.open_floor: I take photos of every stage of the waterproofing for the customer and the housing company. It saves trouble later if there is a leak.
answers.looking_for: I want steady renovation work from a bigger contractor, or subcontracting for several, because it's hard to find customers all year round. English or Finnish for work, and Finnish is fine with customers. On site. I can start after my current job, in about three weeks.

probes: For the levelling I set the laser to the drain height and marked the walls, mixed a self-levelling compound for the low corner and checked the fall with the long level every ten centimetres. It took one day to dry before the waterproofing.
For the water test I closed the drain with a plug and filled the floor with two centimetres of water. I marked the water line on the wall with tape and checked it the next day, and it hadn't dropped.
